subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` `started` mean the user turn is already durable in the transcript, or is UI-only optimistic preservation acceptable while runtime/fallback persistence happens later?
rationale: Changing the ACK boundary affects session-state and duplicate-suppression contracts across Gateway, Pi/native runners, and WebChat history reconciliation, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Make started durable
options.body: Require the Gateway to persist or reserve the user turn before returning `started`, using the shared recorder/session APIs and compatibility tests for duplicate suppression.

options.title: Keep started non-durable
options.body: Leave ACK timing unchanged but document the non-durable contract and rely on UI preservation plus later recovery/failure notices.

options.title: Land a narrower partial fix
options.body: Merge only the WebChat display preservation already present on main and keep Gateway durability as a separate canonical issue or PR.

recommendation.title: Make started durable
recommendation.body: Require the Gateway to persist or reserve the user turn before returning `started`, using the shared recorder/session APIs and compatibility tests for duplicate suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely original non-blocking ACK change is the central product contract being revisited.
